title: BJP Wins West Bengal for First Time in Party's 46-Year History
detail: The Bharatiya Janata Party secured 206 of 294 assembly seats in West Bengal state elections, making history as the first time in BJP's existence it has won the state. The landslide victory ended Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee's Trinamool Congress (TMC) after 15 years in power. PM Modi called it the most consequential state election win since 2014. Analysts attributed the result to nationalist sentiment following the first anniversary of the Pahalgam terror attack, anti-incumbency against TMC, and sustained ground-level BJP organization over a decade. Mamata Banerjee conceded defeat.

media.caption: BJP wins West Bengal for first time in party history, ending 15-year TMC rule

title: India's Last Communist State Government Falls in Kerala
detail: Kerala voters ended five decades of left-wing governance, ousting the Left Democratic Front (LDF) state government in assembly elections. The defeat marks the end of the last communist-run state government in India, a milestone in the country's post-independence political evolution. The Congress-led United Democratic Front (UDF) returned to power. The result is particularly significant as Kerala had alternated between left and Congress coalitions every five years — this cycle ending communist rule entirely breaks that pattern and shifts India's political map further from the left.

media.caption: Kerala ends five decades of left-wing rule as Congress coalition wins state election
